subject: Literature
title: Shakespeare the Businessman
description: A 60-second lesson on Shakespeare the Businessman.

hook.text: Shakespeare was not a starving artist. He was one of the shrewdest businessmen in Elizabethan England.

buildup.text: He invested theatre profits into real estate, grain hoarding, and money lending back in Stratford.

discovery.text: He bought the second-largest house in Stratford and applied for a coat of arms to become a gentleman.

twist.text: He once sued a neighbor over a small debt, revealing a ruthless financial side that surprises modern admirers.

climax.text: Shakespeare retired wealthy to Stratford, proving that artistic genius and business savvy can coexist.

punchline.text: The greatest poet was also a landlord and grain dealer.

quiz.question: How did Shakespeare build his wealth?
options: Solely through writing and publishing plays
Through real estate, grain hoarding, and money lending
